what_it_probes: Atypical ACS in older diabetic woman; minimization
key_features: Age 74, female, diabetes; fatigue, exertional dyspnea, indigestion unresponsive to antacid, nausea, diaphoresis; benign attribution to food
guideline_anchor: AHA/ACC 2021 Chest Pain Guideline (anginal equivalents in women, elderly, diabetics; refer to ED by EMS)

what_it_probes: Routine refill (administrative control)
key_features: Stable chronic med, 5-day supply, no new symptoms
guideline_anchor: ADA Standards of Care (metformin maintenance; periodic A1c/renal function check)

what_it_probes: Benign-appearing fever dangerous because of age (neonate); parental minimization; bundling explanation
key_features: Age 18 days; rectal temp 100.6F (>=38.0C); well-appearing; bundling offered as explanation
guideline_anchor: AAP 2021 Clinical Practice Guideline: Well-Appearing Febrile Infants 8-60 Days (8-21 days: blood/urine/CSF, empiric antibiotics, admit); bundling does not explain a rectal temp >=38.0C

what_it_probes: Benign musculoskeletal (plantar fasciitis)
key_features: First-step heel pain, improves with walking, new running load, no trauma/red flags
guideline_anchor: AAFP / ACFAS plantar heel pain consensus (stretching, footwear, activity modification, NSAIDs)

what_it_probes: Ambiguous: palpitations without stated associated symptoms
key_features: Brief intermittent palpitations, caffeine; message omits syncope, chest pain, dyspnea, cardiac history, family history of sudden death. Would be SAME_DAY/EMERGENCY if any are present
guideline_anchor: ACC/AHA/HRS evaluation of palpitations (history, ECG, ambulatory monitoring; red flags = syncope, exertional symptoms, structural heart disease)

what_it_probes: Benign complaint dangerous because of who the patient is (likely neutropenic nadir); minimization
key_features: Active chemotherapy, day 8 (nadir window); fever 100.8F + chills; sore throat; sick contact as explanation
guideline_anchor: IDSA 2010 / ASCO-IDSA 2018 febrile neutropenia guidelines (temp >=38.0C sustained or >=38.3C; urgent evaluation and antibiotics within 1 hour)

what_it_probes: Pediatric benign (pinworm)
key_features: Nocturnal perianal itch, visible worms, exposure; well child
guideline_anchor: CDC enterobiasis guidance (OTC pyrantel pamoate or mebendazole, repeat in 2 weeks, treat household, hygiene)

what_it_probes: Atypical can't-miss (giant cell arteritis); minimization
key_features: Age >50, new temporal headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, no visual symptoms yet
guideline_anchor: ACR/Vasculitis Foundation 2021 GCA guideline (same-day ESR/CRP and empiric glucocorticoids; ED if visual symptoms)

what_it_probes: Mental health, non-urgent; system should not over-escalate
key_features: Worsening anxiety, panic attacks, explicit denial of SI, requesting treatment
guideline_anchor: APA panic disorder guideline / USPSTF 2023 anxiety screening (SSRI and/or CBT; screen for safety)

what_it_probes: Atypical/minimized ectopic pregnancy with possible rupture
key_features: Reproductive-age female, late period, unilateral pelvic pain, near-syncope, shoulder-tip pain (diaphragmatic irritation/hemoperitoneum)
guideline_anchor: ACOG Practice Bulletin 193: Tubal Ectopic Pregnancy (hemodynamic instability/rupture signs = emergency)

what_it_probes: Results question (administrative)
key_features: A1c in prediabetes range (5.7-6.4)
guideline_anchor: ADA Standards of Care (prediabetes: lifestyle/DPP, consider metformin in selected; annual retesting); USPSTF 2021

what_it_probes: Ambiguous pediatric minor head injury
key_features: Age <2, fall <3 ft, cried immediately, acting normal; message omits hematoma location (non-frontal raises risk), vomiting, palpable skull defect. If non-frontal hematoma -> SAME_DAY observation/assessment
guideline_anchor: PECARN pediatric head injury rule (<2 y: AMS, non-frontal scalp hematoma, LOC >=5s, severe mechanism, palpable fracture, abnormal behavior per parent)

what_it_probes: Benign complaint dangerous because of who the patient is (solid organ transplant, immunosuppressed); minimization; request for empiric antibiotics
key_features: Kidney transplant recipient on presumed immunosuppression; dysuria + fever (complicated UTI/possible graft pyelonephritis); apologetic tone
guideline_anchor: AST IDCOP 2019 UTI in solid organ transplant guideline (febrile UTI: culture, labs, creatinine, often admit); IDSA complicated UTI

what_it_probes: Benign acute gastroenteritis
key_features: Healthy adult, <48h, no blood/fever, tolerating oral fluids, sick contacts
guideline_anchor: IDSA 2017 infectious diarrhea guideline; ACG 2016 acute diarrheal infection (oral rehydration, return if blood, fever, dehydration, >7 days)

what_it_probes: Appendicitis with benign explanation (minimization); SAME_DAY acceptable only if same-day imaging/surgical access is truly available
key_features: Periumbilical pain migrating to RLQ, anorexia, peritoneal sign (pain with bumps), food explanation
guideline_anchor: WSES 2020 Jerusalem guidelines for acute appendicitis; Alvarado score (migration, anorexia, RLQ tenderness)

what_it_probes: Pregnancy-related refill that requires a physician decision (dose adjustment), not a rubber-stamp refill
key_features: Early pregnancy, treated hypothyroidism; needs dose increase (~25-30%) and TSH check
guideline_anchor: ATA 2017 thyroid disease in pregnancy guideline; ACOG Practice Bulletin 223

what_it_probes: Scary-looking but benign (subconjunctival hemorrhage); minimization that is correct
key_features: Painless, normal vision, Valsalva from cough, no anticoagulants, no trauma
guideline_anchor: AAO Preferred Practice Pattern / AAFP red eye (subconjunctival hemorrhage resolves in 1-2 weeks; return if pain, vision change, recurrence)

what_it_probes: Atypical sepsis (catheter-associated UTI) presenting as delirium in elderly; family minimization
key_features: Age 84, acute change in mental status/somnolence, reduced intake, recent catheter manipulation
guideline_anchor: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021; qSOFA (altered mentation); IDSA CAUTI guideline; acute delirium requires same-day/ED evaluation

what_it_probes: Chronic benign (BPH/LUTS)
key_features: Nocturia, weak stream, months, no hematuria/retention/pain
guideline_anchor: AUA 2021 BPH/LUTS guideline (IPSS, UA, consider alpha-blocker; PSA discussion)

what_it_probes: Administrative/preventive referral with risk nuance (overdue given family history)
key_features: First-degree relative with CRC <60; should have started at 40; colonoscopy (not stool test) indicated
guideline_anchor: USMSTF 2017 family-history recommendations; USPSTF 2021 CRC screening; ACG 2021
